companies.name: AstraZeneca
companies.description: Global biopharmaceutical company focused on oncology, cardiovascular, renal, respiratory and rare-disease medicines.

companies.name: GSK
companies.description: Biopharma company developing vaccines and specialty medicines, especially in infectious diseases, HIV, respiratory and oncology. Its consumer health arm was spun off as Haleon in 2022.

companies.name: Smith & Nephew
companies.description: Medical technology company making orthopaedic implants (hips and knees), sports-medicine devices and advanced wound care products.

companies.name: Shell
companies.description: Integrated energy company that explores for and produces oil and gas, is one of the world's largest LNG traders, and runs a global network of fuel stations.

companies.name: BP
companies.description: Integrated oil and gas company with upstream production, refining and trading, plus fuel retail and lubricants.

companies.name: HSBC Holdings
companies.description: One of the world's largest banks, with most of its profits earned in Asia, especially Hong Kong. Offers retail, commercial and investment banking and wealth management.

companies.name: Barclays
companies.description: British universal bank combining UK retail banking and credit cards with a large global investment bank.

companies.name: Lloyds Banking Group
companies.description: The UK's largest retail bank and mortgage lender, focused almost entirely on the domestic market.

companies.name: NatWest Group
companies.description: UK-focused retail and commercial bank, formerly Royal Bank of Scotland Group, which was bailed out by the government in 2008.

companies.name: Standard Chartered
companies.description: London-headquartered bank that does almost all of its business in Asia, Africa and the Middle East, with a focus on trade finance and wealth management.

companies.name: London Stock Exchange Group
companies.description: Runs the London Stock Exchange but earns most of its revenue from financial data and analytics, index licensing and clearing.

companies.name: Prudential
companies.description: Life and health insurer and asset manager focused on Asia and Africa. Not related to the US company Prudential Financial.

companies.name: Legal & General
companies.description: Insurer and asset manager best known for pension risk transfer (buying out company pension schemes), life insurance and index-tracking funds.

companies.name: Aviva
companies.description: The UK's largest multi-line insurer, selling car, home, life and health insurance, pensions and savings. Bought Direct Line Group in 2025.

companies.name: Admiral Group
companies.description: Car and home insurer that sells mostly online and directly to customers, the largest motor insurer in the UK.

companies.name: 3i Group
companies.description: Private equity and infrastructure investor. Most of its value comes from one holding: the European discount retailer Action.

companies.name: Unilever
companies.description: Consumer goods giant selling beauty, personal care, home care and food products in around 190 countries. Its ice cream business was spun off as The Magnum Ice Cream Company.

companies.name: Haleon
companies.description: Consumer healthcare company spun off from GSK in 2022, selling over-the-counter medicines, oral health and vitamin brands.

companies.name: Reckitt Benckiser
companies.description: Maker of hygiene, cleaning and over-the-counter health brands.

companies.name: Diageo
companies.description: The world's largest spirits company by sales, also brewing Guinness.

companies.name: British American Tobacco
companies.description: One of the world's largest tobacco companies, selling cigarettes plus vapes, heated tobacco and nicotine pouches.

companies.name: Imperial Brands
companies.description: Tobacco company selling cigarettes, fine-cut tobacco, rolling papers and vapes, with major markets in the US, UK, Germany, Spain and Australia.

companies.name: Tesco
companies.description: The UK's largest supermarket chain, with over a quarter of the grocery market, plus wholesale and operations in Ireland and Central Europe.

companies.name: J Sainsbury
companies.description: The UK's second-largest supermarket chain, which also owns the general merchandise retailer Argos.

companies.name: Associated British Foods
companies.description: Diversified group with food, sugar and ingredients businesses, which also owns the discount fashion retailer Primark.

companies.name: Coca-Cola HBC
companies.description: Bottler and distributor of Coca-Cola drinks across Central and Eastern Europe, Italy, Ireland, Nigeria and Egypt.

companies.name: Rio Tinto
companies.description: One of the world's largest miners, earning most of its profit from iron ore in Western Australia, plus aluminium, copper and lithium.

companies.name: Glencore
companies.description: Combines mining (copper, cobalt, zinc, nickel and coal) with one of the world's largest commodity trading businesses.

companies.name: Anglo American
companies.description: Miner refocusing on copper and iron ore after spinning off its platinum business and putting diamonds up for sale.

companies.name: Antofagasta
companies.description: Copper miner controlled by Chile's Luksic family, with all of its mines in Chile.

companies.name: RELX
companies.description: Information and analytics company serving scientists, lawyers, insurers and businesses, plus large trade exhibitions.

companies.name: Compass Group
companies.description: The world's largest contract caterer, running canteens and food service for offices, schools, hospitals, sports stadiums and remote sites. Most of its revenue comes from North America.

companies.name: Next
companies.description: Clothing and homeware retailer with a large online business. It also runs online platforms for other brands and owns several of them outright or in part.

companies.name: Kingfisher
companies.description: Home improvement and DIY retailer with chains in the UK, France and Poland.

companies.name: Pearson
companies.description: Education company providing assessments and qualifications, professional certification testing, English-language learning and digital courseware.

companies.name: International Airlines Group
companies.description: Airline group formed by the 2011 merger of British Airways and Iberia, operating full-service and low-cost carriers.

companies.name: Barratt Redrow
companies.description: The UK's largest housebuilder, formed when Barratt Developments acquired Redrow in 2024.

companies.name: Rolls-Royce Holdings
companies.description: Makes jet engines for widebody airliners and military aircraft, nuclear submarine reactors and large power systems. It does not make Rolls-Royce cars, which belong to BMW.

companies.name: BAE Systems
companies.description: Europe's largest defence contractor, building combat aircraft, submarines, warships, armoured vehicles, munitions and electronics. Has a large US business.

companies.name: Experian
companies.description: One of the three big global credit bureaus, holding credit data on consumers and businesses and selling analytics, fraud prevention and credit scores.

companies.name: Vodafone Group
companies.description: Mobile and broadband operator across Europe and Africa. Its UK business merged with Three in 2025 to form VodafoneThree.

companies.name: BT Group
companies.description: The UK's largest broadband and mobile provider, and owner of Openreach, which runs most of the UK's phone and broadband lines.

companies.name: National Grid
companies.description: Owns the high-voltage electricity transmission network in England and Wales, local electricity distribution in the Midlands and South West, and energy networks in the north-eastern US.

companies.name: SSE
companies.description: Scottish energy company building offshore wind and other renewables, and owning electricity networks in northern Scotland and southern England.

companies.name: Centrica
companies.description: Energy supplier and services company that owns British Gas, the UK's largest household energy supplier, plus energy trading and gas storage.

companies.name: Severn Trent
companies.description: Regulated water and sewerage company serving millions of customers across the Midlands and mid-Wales.

companies.name: Land Securities Group
companies.description: One of the UK's largest commercial property companies (a REIT), owning central London offices, major shopping centres and mixed-use developments.

companies.name: Segro
companies.description: REIT that owns and develops warehouses, logistics sheds and data-centre sites in the UK and continental Europe.

companies.name: Sage Group
companies.description: Provides cloud accounting, payroll and HR software for small and medium-sized businesses.
